description.html: Quartz gravel is a substrate with a coarser grain than sand, and the dark color of the grains gives the bottom depth and makes lighter fish and green plants stand out. Like quartz sand, it is chemically neutral and does not change the pH or hardness of the water, so it is suitable for all freshwater aquariums.

Because of the larger grains, water flows through the substrate more easily, and the heavier grains are not easily stirred up by a strong filter current. Food leftovers settle between the grains, where they are easy to remove with a gravel vacuum during regular maintenance.

Before putting it in the aquarium, rinse the gravel well under running water until the water runs clear. It can be used on its own or combined with quartz sand, for example sand in front and gravel at the back or around roots and stones. The 1 kg pack is enough for a small aquarium, topping up the bottom or decorative zones. Clean the bottom with a gravel vacuum at every partial water change. If you are just setting up an aquarium, read our beginner aquariums guide.
